findings.title: API route has no authentication check
findings.description: This API route defines a mutating handler (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) that writes to the database, with no recognisable auth or session check inside it. It may allow unauthorised data changes.
findings.remediation: Verify the session or user at the top of the handler (Clerk auth(), Supabase getUser(), getServerSession) and return 401/403 when unauthorised. If the endpoint really is public, document it explicitly.

findings.title: Missing security header: Content-Security-Policy
findings.description: Headers are declared somewhere, but Content-Security-Policy appears in none of them (next.config, middleware/proxy, vercel.json, _headers).
findings.remediation: Add Content-Security-Policy inside next.config headers(). Use a strict CSP, X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN, and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

findings.title: Security decision relies on a spoofable X-Forwarded-For
findings.description: app/api/auth/register/route.ts reads X-Forwarded-For in a security decision (rate limit, attempt counter, allowlist). XFF is sent by the CLIENT, and reverse proxies often do not overwrite it — an attacker sends a different XFF on every request and BYPASSES the IP-based limit entirely (every attempt counts as a new IP).
findings.remediation: In security decisions, use the header your reverse proxy sets RELIABLY okuyun (Caddy: X-Real-IP {remote_host}; nginx: $remote_addr / real_ip module; Express: app.set('trust proxy', ...) with req.ip). Never TRUST the first value of the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For.

findings.title: ReDoS: regular expression built from user input
findings.description: new RegExp() is called with a non-literal pattern. If the pattern comes from user input, an attacker can supply a catastrophic pattern and stall the event loop.
findings.remediation: Never build a regex from user input. Use a fixed pattern and match the input against it, or escape user input before embedding.

findings.title: Tarih/ay değeri toISOString() ile üretiliyor (saat dilimine göre gün kayar)
findings.description: lib/booking-validation.ts:29 — "bugün" değeri `new Date().toISOString()` ile, yani UTC gününden üretiliyor. UTC+3'te gece 00:00–03:00 arasında bu değer DÜNÜ gösterir: o saatlerde oluşturulan kayıt yanlış güne yazılır, abonelik/deneme bitişi ve fatura tarihi bir gün kayabilir.
findings.remediation: Tarih-only aritmetiğini saat diliminden bağımsız yapın: parçaları ayırıp `Date.UTC(y, m-1, d + n)` ile hesaplayın ve sonucu `getUTCFullYear/Month/Date` ile biçimlendirin. "Bugün" için işletmenin bölgesini sabitleyin: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-CA", { timeZone: "Europe/Istanbul", ... })` (en-CA zaten YYYY-MM-DD verir). Bu yardımcıları TEK bir modülde tutun ve kopyalarını arayın — düzeltilmiş bir yardımcının kopyası sessizce bozuk kalır.

findings.title: The authorisation check runs after input validation
findings.description: In `app/api/upload/route.ts` the authorisation check comes after input validation. An unauthorised caller learns the schema first, and the gate itself cannot be tested without constructing a valid body.
findings.remediation: Move the gate first: read only the field the authorisation decision needs (e.g. `resource`), run the check, then do the full validation.

findings.title: State-changing route has no CSRF protection
findings.description: This state-changing handler has no explicit CSRF token check. It does expect a JSON body, and the session library uses the SameSite=Lax cookie default: a cross-site form cannot construct this request, and a preflighted JSON request carries no cookie. So it is NOT exploitable today — but the protection rests on a cookie default rather than an explicit check. Loosening SameSite, or accepting form bodies, opens it.
findings.remediation: Add CSRF token validation (double-submit cookie or a server-generated token). Use SameSite=Lax/Strict cookies and validate the Origin/Referer header. Where possible use an Authorization: Bearer token instead of a cookie.

findings.title: No rate limiting or brute-force protection on a sensitive endpoint
findings.description: No rate limiting is visible on this sensitive endpoint (app/(auth)/forgot-password/actions.ts). The project does have rate-limit infrastructure, but it could not be confirmed on this route.
findings.remediation: Add IP and identity based rate limiting to login, OTP and payment endpoints (e.g. @upstash/ratelimit), cap failed attempts, and add a CAPTCHA or delay if needed.

findings.title: Persisted or external JSON parsed without a guard (one bad record kills the job)
findings.description: app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:30 JSON'u try/except olmadan parse ediyor. If the argument comes from a persisted column or an external response, a single malformed record takes down the whole request or job — and it fails where the data is READ, not where it was WRITTEN, which makes it hard to diagnose.
findings.remediation: Wrap the parse in try/except (JSONDecodeError / SyntaxError); fall back to a safe default (empty list or dict) on failure, skip the record and log it. One bad row then cannot bring down the entire run.

findings.title: Security decision relies on a spoofable X-Forwarded-For
findings.description: lib/ratelimit.ts reads X-Forwarded-For in a security decision (rate limit, attempt counter, allowlist). XFF is sent by the CLIENT, and reverse proxies often do not overwrite it — an attacker sends a different XFF on every request and BYPASSES the IP-based limit entirely (every attempt counts as a new IP). The file also appears to read a trusted IP source; confirm the two are not mixed up.
findings.remediation: In security decisions, use the header your reverse proxy sets RELIABLY okuyun (Caddy: X-Real-IP {remote_host}; nginx: $remote_addr / real_ip module; Express: app.set('trust proxy', ...) with req.ip). Never TRUST the first value of the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For.

findings.remediation: Record successful and failed auth and payment events (user, IP, timestamp, outcome) with a structured logger, and alert on anomalies.

findings.title: No security.txt (RFC 9116)
findings.description: The project has no /.well-known/security.txt. That file declares a contact channel so security researchers can disclose issues responsibly (RFC 9116).
findings.remediation: Add public/.well-known/security.txt with Contact and Expires fields, and preferably Encryption and Policy too.
findings.remediationCode:
Contact: mailto:security@example.com
Expires: 2027-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
Preferred-Languages: tr, en

checks.title: Rate limiting in place
checks.detail: Rate limiting found (11 match(es)).
checks.remediation: Add IP + identity based rate limiting to API and form endpoints (@upstash/ratelimit for Next.js, express-rate-limit for Express). Cover login, contact and payment endpoints at minimum.

evidence.snippet: - The built-in public-route rate limiter is process-local; a distributed deployment should use a shared store such as Redis.

checks.title: API routes behind an auth guard
checks.detail: 2 route(s) that WRITE to the database carry no auth signal (2 suspicious routes in total). Unless these are deliberately public this is a serious hole — verify by hand.
checks.remediation: Verify the session or user at the top of the handler (Clerk auth(), Supabase getUser(), getServerSession) and return 401/403 when unauthorised. Document endpoints that are genuinely public.

checks.title: .env protected (gitignored, never committed)
checks.detail: .gitignore covers .env and no .env file is tracked.
checks.remediation: Add `.env*` (and `!.env.example`) to .gitignore. If a .env was committed, untrack it with `git rm --cached`, purge it from history and rotate EVERY secret it held.

checks.title: No secrets hardcoded in source
checks.detail: No known provider pattern and no high-entropy embedded secret found.
checks.remediation: Move secrets into .env and read them via process.env; revoke and reissue any exposed key from the provider dashboard.

checks.title: Security headers configured
checks.detail: Missing headers: Content-Security-Policy (looked in: next.config.ts, vercel.json, proxy.ts).
checks.remediation: Declare CSP, X-Frame-Options: DENY/SAMEORIGIN, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Strict-Transport-Security and Referrer-Policy in next.config headers() (or the vercel.json "headers" block).

checks.title: Supabase RLS policies declared
checks.detail: This project does not use Supabase.
checks.remediation: Declare `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` plus matching `CREATE POLICY` for every table, and commit them as migrations instead of leaving them in the dashboard.

checks.title: Input validation in place
checks.detail: No known schema validation library found. Validation may be hand-written — review the body handling in your API endpoints.
checks.remediation: Validate with a schema library such as zod in API routes and form handlers (`schema.safeParse(body)`), and never pass an unvalidated body to the database.

checks.title: Vercel region pinned (aligned with the database)
checks.detail: Region pinned: iad1. Confirm manually that it matches the database region (not statically detectable).
checks.remediation: Add your database's region to vercel.json, e.g. `"regions": ["fra1"]` (Supabase eu-central → fra1/dub1, us-east → iad1). Check the project region in the Supabase dashboard.

checks.title: No sequential query chains per page
checks.detail: 7 file(s) have 5+ awaits and no Promise.all: app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts (8 await), app/api/book/route.ts (7 await), app/api/auth/register/route.ts (7 await), app/(dashboard)/staff/page.tsx (6 await), app/api/portal/route.ts (5 await). Parallelise them if they are independent; ignore if they are genuinely sequential (heuristic check).
checks.remediation: Count the await chain on the page and parallelise independent queries with `const [a, b, c] = await Promise.all([...])`. Collapse repeated auth/role lookups with React cache(). Prove the fix with a TTFB measurement.

checks.title: loading.tsx iskeletleri var
checks.detail: The app router has 54 page(s) and no loading.tsx at all — users stare at a blank screen while server queries run.
checks.remediation: Add loading.tsx under app/ (at least at the root and in data-fetching route groups) and render a skeleton — the Suspense boundary is created for you.

checks.title: No select * on heavy list queries
checks.detail: select * is used in 1 place(s). Harmless on small tables — narrow the ones behind heavy list queries.
checks.remediation: Select only the columns you need: `.select("id, name, created_at")`. To count rows use `select("*", { count: "exact", head: true })`.

evidence.snippet: FOR rec IN SELECT * FROM jsonb_each_text(scoped) LOOP

checks.title: Status shown on screen is measured
checks.detail: Health and connection status come from a real measurement, not a hardcoded value.
checks.remediation: Derive the value from a measurement: open the connection, probe the service. If it cannot be measured, return 'unknown'.

checks.title: Guards passed a negative test
checks.detail: Was every protective test watched FAILING once the thing it protects was deliberately broken?
checks.remediation: Remove the guard, run the test, watch it fail, put the guard back. A passing test is no proof that it measures anything.

checks.title: Reported numbers are derived from their source
checks.detail: Do the counters in tests and in the UI come from a measurement rather than a hand-written constant?
checks.remediation: Derive the number from the file or schema that produces it. A hand-written counter keeps passing after the thing it counts disappears.

checks.title: Revoking access also ends open sessions
checks.detail: Password changes and access revocations also invalidate that person's open sessions.
checks.remediation: Every path that revokes access should call session invalidation, while keeping the acting user's own session alive.

checks.title: Immutability guards cover both UPDATE and DELETE
checks.detail: Every table closed to updates is closed to deletes too.
checks.remediation: Write the DELETE counterpart of every immutability trigger, and allow corrections through a reversing entry.

checks.title: The data scoper derives its keys
checks.detail: Scoping does not depend on a hand-listed set of keys; a new collection is covered automatically.
checks.remediation: Derive the keys from the schema or type, and write a leak test that walks the entire response.

checks.title: Backups pass a restore rehearsal
checks.detail: The dump is verified by restoring it into a throwaway database.
checks.remediation: Restore the dump, count the tables, verify the constraints. A backup is not 'taken' until the rehearsal passes.

checks.title: The monitor has an alert target
checks.detail: Not meaningful for this project.
checks.remediation: Configure an alert target — a monitor without one just reports to itself.

checks.title: The monitor's LAST RUN result was read
checks.detail: Was the last run confirmed SUCCESSFUL, rather than merely confirming the timer exists?
checks.remediation: Run `systemctl is-failed <service>` or its equivalent. A timer existing says nothing about the run passing.

checks.title: Health endpoints were called by hand
checks.detail: Were the production health endpoints actually requested (do they return 200)?
checks.remediation: A single curl is enough. Seeing them defined is not seeing them answer.

checks.title: Dependent services actually respond
checks.detail: Were dependencies like the scanner, queue or cache exercised with a real operation?
checks.remediation: Measure BEHAVIOUR, not configuration: run a real scan or queue job.

checks.title: No page is statically generated under a strict-dynamic CSP
checks.detail: Pages are tied to request time, so a CSP nonce can be emitted.
checks.remediation: Bind the page to the request with `connection()` or `force-dynamic`; afterwards the script count must equal the nonce count.

checks.title: The product was opened in a browser and looked at
checks.detail: Were the screens actually opened and read (rather than trusting a text scan)?
checks.remediation: Open the page, check the console, compare script and nonce counts. Three detectors can say 'clean' while the screen says otherwise.

checks.title: Malware scanning happens BEFORE the write
checks.detail: An uploaded file is scanned before it is written to storage.
checks.remediation: Scan first and never write bytes that did not come back clean.

checks.title: The bucket's public URL is disabled
checks.detail: Was the bucket's public URL (e.g. Cloudflare `r2.dev`) confirmed DISABLED in the provider dashboard?
checks.remediation: Check it in the provider dashboard. This switch cannot be tested from outside, and while it is on every document and backup is world-readable.

checks.title: No hand edits inside generated files
checks.detail: Nothing is hand-added to generated files; anything extra lives in a separate additions file.
checks.remediation: Move hand-written content into its own file, have the generator include it, and test that it survives regeneration.

checks.title: The test command does not enumerate files by hand
checks.detail: Tests are collected with a glob, so a new test file runs on its own.
checks.remediation: Use a glob. A hand-written list silently skips every new test someone forgets to add.
